docs.title: Check the install
docs.text:
from cmb_lensing.simulate import load_sim
data_set = load_sim(nside = 64, theta_pix = 5, pol = "I", master_seed = 1)
print(f"Pixel resolution = {data_set.theta_pix} arcminutes per pixel")

If you wish to run the unit tests or actively contribute to the development of the repository it will also be necessary to have juliacall installed and a CMBLensing.jl checkout - see Developing for more information.

docs.title: Downloading the CAMB grid
docs.text:
sample_joint needs the theory power spectra at every proposed LCDM parameter combination. It gets them from a precomputed grid of real CAMB spectra: a 5D tensor-product cubic spline over (H0, logA, ns, ombh2, omch2), stored in camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz (~7.9 GB). It serves any subset of the five parameters and every polarization mode.

This file is too large to store on GitHub. It is hosted on the Hugging Face dataset zaneblood1/cmb_lensing_data and is downloaded automatically into camb_splines/ the first time the code needs it (cmb_lensing/camb_splines.py). No manual setup is needed.

To fetch it ahead of time, run the following command in a bash terminal from the repo root:

cmb-lensing-download-splines

On a cluster, run this once on a login node: compute nodes often have no internet access. To use your own grid instead, rebuild it on the cluster (Building the CAMB Grid), copy it back to your local machine and place it at camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz.

The same Hugging Face dataset holds the chains, phi noise, delensed covariance and map_joint comparison outputs. None of those are downloaded automatically; see Data Availability.

docs.title: Validating the grid
docs.text:
python tests/test_camb_grid.py --grid camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz -n 20

compares the spline against direct CAMB at random interior points. Typical max |Δ ln Cl| is ~1e-3 (TT) to ~5e-3 (EE near an acoustic trough).

docs.title: HPC setup
docs.text:
All cluster scripts are Slurm scripts, used for e.g. sampling LCDM parameters en masse or generating data for Fisher forecasting. Before running any of them, make a copy of the hpc_local.example.sh script at the repository root and fill it in with your own cluster configuration. The copy is gitignored to avoid sharing personal email accounts, etc.

cp hpc_local.example.sh hpc_local.sh

then edit hpc_local.sh:

#the conda install and environment the jobs run in
source /path/to/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate myenv

#where Slurm mails job failures
export SBATCH_MAIL_USER=you@example.edu

#the CMBLensing.jl checkout, used only by runtime_comparison/
export CMBLENSING_JL_PATH=/path/to/CMBLensing.jl

Every driver and every job script it submits sources this file.

docs.title: How the drivers work
docs.text:
Each pipeline folder has a driver that only submits jobs, and is run with bash, not sbatch:

bash get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh

A driver can be run from any directory. It cds into its own folder, sources the repo-root hpc_local.sh and hpc_submit.sh and submits its job script once per job. The physical configuration (nside, theta_pix, noise_level, l_knee, ...) is set by passing flags to each driver, e.g. bash get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh --nside=128 --noise_level=5; a setting that is not passed keeps the default listed at the top of the driver. Keep them the same across drivers for one experiment, so the chains, the phi-noise measurements and the forecasts all describe the same box.

Driver What it does camb_grid_generation/camb_grid.sh Computes the CAMB spectra on the 5D parameter grid that sample_joint interpolates. Only needed to rebuild the grid instead of downloading it (Building the CAMB Grid). get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh Runs the LCDM sampler on many simulated data maps, with several chains per map. These chains are the main result (LCDM Sampling on the HPC). measure_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise.sh Runs map_joint on many realizations to measure the noise of its lensing potential estimate. Used as the forecast's phi noise (Measuring Noise in the MAP Estimates). measure_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise.sh Runs chains with the LCDM parameters held fixed to measure the noise of the sampler's lensing potential estimate. Also usable as the forecast's phi noise (Measuring Noise in the Sampler). get_delensed_field_covariance/get_delensed_field_covariance.sh Measures the covariance of the delensed field and how it changes with each parameter. The Fisher forecast cannot run without it (Computing Delensed Covariance Matrices). runtime_comparison/run_performance_test.sh Times map_joint in Python against CMBLensing.jl over a range of map sizes.

docs.title: Submission throttle
docs.text:
Some clusters cancel every submission beyond a cap on queued jobs instead of leaving it pending. Every driver therefore submits through submit_throttled (repo-root hpc_submit.sh): before each sbatch it waits until you have fewer than MAX_QUEUED_JOBS jobs queued or running (default 85), checking every SUBMIT_POLL_SECONDS (default 60), and it retries a rejected sbatch. Set EXCLUDE_NODES in hpc_local.sh (comma separated, e.g. ac006) to keep every job a driver submits off those nodes: it is passed as sbatch --exclude, since sbatch reads no environment variable for it. Override either value in hpc_local.sh.

A driver therefore runs until its last job is submitted, which can take hours. Keep it alive after you log out:

nohup bash get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh > submit.log 2>&1 &
tail -f submit.log

nohup ignores the hangup signal sent at logout, > submit.log 2>&1 sends output and errors to the file, and & runs it in the background. Alternatively run the driver inside tmux, detach with Ctrl-b d, and reattach later with tmux attach (on the same login node).

Neither survives a reboot of the login node. Every driver can be run again with the same flags after such an interruption: it records each job it submits as an empty file in <output folder>/submitted/ and skips those, so only the missing jobs are submitted. A job that timed out or failed is skipped too; delete its file in submitted/ to have it submitted again.

hpc_local.example.sh also defines two shortcuts for the login shell. Add source /path/to/CMBLensing.py/hpc_local.sh to your ~/.bashrc to have them at every login:

#the nohup line above; the output goes to get_lcdm_samples/submit_lcdm_5uk.log
run_driver get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh --noise_level=5 --out_dir_name=lcdm_5uk

kill_driver               #list the running drivers
kill_driver lcdm_5uk      #stop the drivers whose command line holds this text

kill_driver stops the driver only; cancel the jobs it already submitted with scancel.

docs.title: Building these docs locally
docs.text:
mkdocs serve      #live-reloading preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build      #static site in site/

docs.title: Building the CAMB Grid
docs.text: Most users should download the grid. Rebuild it when CAMB is upgraded or the grid's box changes.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
The 5D CAMB spline is used to interpolate real CAMB spectra on a tensor-product grid over (H0, logA, ns, ombh2, omch2) with (tau = 0.05, mnu = 0.06, r = 0), evaluated in log spectra space (cmb_lensing/camb_grid_interp.py). The grid is laid out in H0 because a rectangular box in theta_MC_100 has corners CAMB cannot solve; the sampler works in theta_MC_100 and converts back and forth through a stored theta(H0, ombh2, omch2) table.

cd camb_grid_generation
bash camb_grid.sh                                            #875 jobs, one 81-point H0 sweep each
python merge_camb_grid.py --grid_dir multi_param_CAMB_grid   #-> multi_param_CAMB_grid/camb_grid_spline.npz
python ../tests/test_camb_grid.py --grid multi_param_CAMB_grid/camb_grid_spline.npz -n 20

Every grid setting has a default in camb_grid.sh and can be overridden on the command line as --<name>=<value>. For example:

bash camb_grid.sh --lmax=5000 --h0_nodes=101 --out_dir_name=grid_lmax_5000

Every run writes the submission date and all setting values to submission_settings.txt in the output folder (replacing any earlier copy), so check that file to see what a grid was built with. Use a new out_dir_name when you change settings.

docs.title: Computing Delensed Covariance Matrices
docs.text:
Measures the empirical per-mode covariance of the delensed field, and its finite difference in theta. It is the field block of the Fisher forecast, which cannot run without it.

Each job uses one seed and runs at every stencil point \(\theta_0\) and \(\theta_0 \pm h_i\):

  1. load_sim(theta) at the chosen pol (common random numbers: at one seed the fields differ only through the cosmology),
  2. inverse-lens the noiseless lensed field by the Wiener-filtered true phi \(W\phi\), with \(W = C_\phi / (C_\phi + N_\phi)\) built once at \(\theta_0\),
  3. store the per-mode covariance \(\mathrm{Re}(X Y^*) / n_\text{side}^2\) of every component on the rfft grid.
pol Stored components I TT P EE, BB IP TT, TE, EE, BB

The merge is the realization mean at each stencil point.

docs.title: Choosing N_phi for the Wiener Filter
docs.text:
Driver Setting What it Controls phi_noise="", qe_filter=unlensed (default) or lensed the box quadratic-estimate \(N^{(0)}\) (the TT estimator for I, the EB estimator for P and IP), with the unlensed or lensed spectra in its filter; the response is always unlensed phi_noise=<path> the nphi of a merged map_joint or sampler phi-noise file

Match it to the forecast it will feed: nothing checks that the file's W was built from the same N_phi as the forecast's phi block.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
bash get_delensed_field_covariance/get_delensed_field_covariance.sh
#copy delensed_covariance_output/ to your machine, then
python get_delensed_field_covariance/merge_delensed_field_covariance.py --covariance_dir <delensed_covariance_output>

Job files written before 2026-11-11 (temperature only, with no pol key) need --legacy_format added to the merge; the merged file is in the current format either way.

Other settings in the driver: pol (I, P or IP; the forecast must use the same), derivative_params (the forecast's --params must be drawn from this list), step_sigma (0.05, in units of PARAM_SIGMA; accurate at nside 128 / 2.5' / 2.5 to 10 uK-arcmin, so for another box or noise level rerun with the step halved and check that the forecast does not change substantially), num_realizations, seed_prefix, out_dir_name (the output folder's name inside get_delensed_field_covariance/). A 3-point temperature job at nside 128 takes ~20 s.

Every setting has a default in the driver and can be overridden on the command line as --<name>=<value>, e.g.

bash get_delensed_field_covariance/get_delensed_field_covariance.sh --noise_level=10 --pol=IP \
    --derivative_params="omch2 logA" --out_dir_name=delensed_covariance_output_IP_10uk

A misspelled name is ignored and the default used. Each run writes the submission date and every setting to submission_settings.txt in the output folder (replacing any earlier copy); use a new out_dir_name when you change settings.

docs.title: Output: delensed_covariance.npz
docs.text:
Key Content pol, components the data's polarization and the stored components, in order delensed_fid the delensed covariance at \(\theta_0\), shape (n_components, nside, nside // 2 + 1) delensed_plus, delensed_minus the same at \(\theta_0 \pm h_i\), shape (n_params, n_components, nside, nside // 2 + 1) names, steps the differentiated parameters (in the package's standard order) and their steps \(h_i\) metadata the box, the stencil points, the seeds and how W was built

Merged temperature files written before 2026-11-11 have no components key and no component axis; the forecast still reads them.

docs.title: LCDM Sampling on the HPC
docs.text:
A single chain on a single data map says little on its own: the map carries cosmic variance, and one chain cannot show whether the sampler has converged. This pipeline therefore runs the LCDM sampler on many simulated data maps, with several chains per map. Averaging over maps removes the cosmic variance of any one map, and comparing the chains of one map checks convergence.

By default it simulates 10 data maps at the ground-truth cosmology and runs 5 chains on each, as 50 separate Slurm jobs. Each map is 128 x 128 pixels of temperature data at 2.5 arcminutes per pixel with 5 uK-arcmin of noise, and each chain runs for 3000 iterations and samples three parameters (omch2, theta_MC_100 and logA).

Before you start, set up the cluster as described in Installation, and tune the proposal widths on a single chain (Running a Single LCDM Chain).

docs.title: Submitting the chains
docs.text:
The driver script submits one job per chain. Run it from the repository root on a login node:

bash get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh

The driver waits whenever too many of your jobs are queued, so it can keep running for a long time. To let it continue after you log out, start it this way instead:

nohup bash get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh > submit.log 2>&1 &

See the submission throttle for details.

docs.title: Changing the settings
docs.text:
Every setting has a default, listed at the top of the driver script. To change one, pass it as a flag of the form --<name>=<value>. For example, this runs at a higher noise level with a wider proposal for one parameter, and writes to its own folder:

bash get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh --noise_level=10 --omch2_proposal_sigma=2e-3 --out_dir_name=run_10uk

Check the spelling of each flag: a misspelled name is not an error. It is ignored and the default is used.

The settings are:

Setting Default Meaning nside, theta_pix 128, 2.5 pixels per map side and arcminutes per pixel noise_level 5 white noise level in uK-arcmin pol I the data the chains see: I (temperature), P (polarization) or IP (both) num_maps, num_chains 10, 5 the number of data maps and of chains per map map_prefix 234567 sets the map seeds: map number m uses the seed map_prefix * m sample_ombh2, sample_omch2, sample_theta_MC_100, sample_log_a, sample_ns omch2, theta_MC_100 and logA are true true or false: whether each parameter is sampled <param>_ground the fiducial cosmology the ground-truth value the data maps are simulated at <param>_min, <param>_max about ±5 sigma around the ground truth the range each parameter is allowed to explore <param>_proposal_sigma 1e-4 (ombh2), 1e-3 (omch2, theta_MC_100), 1e-2 (log_a, ns) the width of each parameter's Metropolis proposal iters_per_chain 3000 iterations per chain num_burn_in_fix_theta 100 initial iterations in which the LCDM parameters are held fixed num_burn_in_always_accept 0 initial iterations in which every lensing potential step is accepted hmc_num_steps, hmc_step_size 10, 0.05 the number and size of the steps in the lensing potential update out_dir_name joint_inference_<submission date> the name of the run's output folder

In the names above, <param> is one of ombh2, omch2, theta_MC_100, log_a and ns.

A sampled parameter starts each chain at a random point in its range. A parameter that is not sampled is held at its ground-truth value.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
The run's folder is created inside the driver's own folder:

get_lcdm_samples/lcdm_sampler_data/<out_dir_name>/

It holds, for every chain, one history file per sampled parameter, with one sample per line:

<param>_map_<map seed>_chain_<chain index>_history.txt

The same folder holds a file named submission_settings.txt, which records the submission date, every setting and the random starting point of each chain. It is rewritten by every run, so use a new out_dir_name whenever you change the settings.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Copy the run's folder to your machine and analyze it as shown in Analyzing Chain Data.

docs.title: Measuring Noise in the MAP Estimates
docs.text: The MAP estimate of the lensing potential is never exact: it differs from the true lensing potential by a reconstruction noise. This pipeline measures that noise for every Fourier mode of the map, at the ground-truth cosmology. The result can be used as the lensing noise of the Fisher forecast, or to build the Wiener filter of the delensed covariance.

docs.title: How the noise is measured
docs.text:
Each job simulates one data map, runs the MAP estimate on it, and compares the estimated lensing potential \(\hat\phi\) with the true one \(\phi_{\rm true}\). For every Fourier mode it stores three numbers:

\[ |\hat\phi|^2, \qquad \mathrm{Re}(\hat\phi\, \phi_{\rm true}^*), \qquad |\phi_{\rm true}|^2 . \]

These are the power of the estimate, the cross power of the estimate with the truth, and the power of the truth.

The merge step averages each of the three over all of the simulated maps. It then forms the squared correlation between the estimate and the truth,

\[ r^2 = \frac{\langle \mathrm{Re}(\hat\phi\, \phi_{\rm true}^*) \rangle^2}{\langle |\hat\phi|^2 \rangle \langle |\phi_{\rm true}|^2 \rangle}, \]

and converts it into a noise level, using the theory spectrum \(C_\phi\) of the lensing potential:

\[ N_\phi = C_\phi \left( \frac{1}{r^2} - 1 \right). \]

A mode that is reconstructed perfectly has \(r^2 = 1\) and no noise. A mode that carries no information has \(r^2\) near 0 and a very large noise. The averages are taken before the ratio, because a ratio of averages is far less noisy than an average of ratios.

The error on the noise is a jackknife: the noise is recomputed with each simulated map left out in turn, and the scatter of those results gives the error.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
By default the pipeline simulates 100 temperature maps of 128 x 128 pixels at 2.5 arcminutes per pixel with 5 uK-arcmin of noise, and submits one Slurm job per map. The settings are changed with flags, as for every driver (see Installation).

Step 1. On the cluster, submit the jobs from the repository root.

bash measure_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise.sh

Step 2. When the jobs have finished, copy the output folder to your machine. It is created inside the driver's own folder:

measure_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise/map_joint_phi_noise_output/

Step 3. Merge the job files into a single file.

python measure_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise/merge_map_joint_phi_noise.py --noise_dir <path to map_joint_phi_noise_output>

The merged file is written into that folder:

map_joint_phi_noise.npz

docs.title: What the merged file holds
docs.text:
Every array is on the same Fourier grid as the maps, with the shape (nside, nside // 2 + 1).

Key Content nphi the noise of every mode. It is NaN where the average cross power is zero or negative, and 0 at the zero mode nphi_error the jackknife error on the noise nphi_leave_one_out the noise recomputed with each map left out, one array per map auto_per_realization, cross_per_realization, true_auto_per_realization the three stored numbers for every map, one array per map. The noise and its error can be rebuilt from them without the job files nside, theta_pix, noise_level, l_knee, pol, param_names, params the map size, resolution, noise settings, data type and cosmology of the run

docs.title: Using the result
docs.text:
Pass the merged file to the Fisher forecast as its lensing noise, together with a delensed covariance:

python -m cmb_lensing.fisher_forecast --noise 5 --delensed_covariance <delensed_covariance.npz> --phi_noise map_joint_phi_noise.npz

The forecast must use the same data type (--pol) as the run that produced the file.

The same file can be given to the delensed covariance pipeline, which then builds its Wiener filter from this noise (see Computing Delensed Covariance Matrices).

To plot the noise as a function of scale, next to the sampler's noise, see Measuring Noise in the Sampler.

docs.title: Measuring Noise in the Sampler
docs.text: The sampler does not return one estimate of the lensing potential but many samples of it, whose average is the posterior mean. This pipeline measures the noise of that posterior mean for every Fourier mode of the map. The result can be used as the lensing noise of the Fisher forecast, or to build the Wiener filter of the delensed covariance.

docs.title: How the noise is measured
docs.text:
Each job simulates one data map and runs a chain on it with the LCDM parameters held at their ground-truth values, so that only the fields and the lensing potential are sampled. Several chains are run per map. The first starts at a lensing potential of zero and the others at random draws, so the chains start far apart.

The merge step removes the burn-in from every chain and averages the remaining samples of each map into its posterior mean \(\bar\phi\). It then averages two quantities over the maps, and takes their ratio:

\[ r^2 = \frac{\langle \mathrm{Re}(\bar\phi\, \phi_{\rm true}^*) \rangle}{\langle |\phi_{\rm true}|^2 \rangle}. \]

This is how strongly the posterior mean responds to the true lensing potential. It is converted into a noise level with the theory spectrum \(C_\phi\) of the lensing potential:

\[ N_\phi = C_\phi \left( \frac{1}{r^2} - 1 \right). \]

This differs from the formula for the MAP estimates, which also uses the power of the estimate, \(\langle |\hat\phi|^2 \rangle\). For an exact posterior mean the two formulas agree. For a finite chain, the power of the posterior mean is inflated by the chain's own sampling error, and the formula here avoids it.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
By default the pipeline simulates 100 temperature maps of 128 x 128 pixels at 2.5 arcminutes per pixel with 5 uK-arcmin of noise, and runs 2 chains of 6000 iterations on each, one Slurm job per chain. The settings are changed with flags, as for every driver (see Installation).

Step 1. On the cluster, submit the chains from the repository root. The driver keeps running until every job is submitted (see the submission throttle).

nohup bash measure_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise.sh > submit.log 2>&1 &

If the driver is interrupted before its last job is submitted (for example by a reboot of the login node), run the same command again with the same flags: chains already submitted are skipped, as for every driver (see the submission throttle).

Step 2. Merge the chains, giving the number of iterations to remove from the start of each chain as burn-in. The merge is itself a Slurm job, submitted from the driver's folder. It can be run while chains are still going: it uses the iterations finished so far.

cd measure_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise
sbatch merge_sampler_phi_noise.sh --burn_in=600

The merged file is written into the output folder:

sampler_phi_noise_output/sampler_phi_noise.npz

Step 3. Check that the burn-in was long enough.

Point the entry of convergence_files in the __main__ block of measure_phi_noise/phi_noise_analysis.py at the merged file, under its noise level, then run the script. It takes no arguments:

python ../phi_noise_analysis.py

Next to the phi noise spectra, this writes sampler_rhat_<noise>uk.png into measure_phi_noise/phi_noise_plots/noise_level_<noise>uk/, a plot that compares the chains of each map with one another, as a function of scale. It shows the Gelman-Rubin statistic, which is close to 1 when the chains agree. Every scale should be below the reference line at 1.01. A scale well above it means the burn-in or the chains were too short there.

docs.title: What the merged file holds
docs.text:
Key Content nphi the noise of every mode. It is NaN where it could not be measured, and 0 at the zero mode nphi_error the jackknife error on the noise nphi_leave_one_out the noise recomputed with each map left out, one array per map rhat_real, rhat_imaginary the Gelman-Rubin statistic of every mode's real and imaginary part, one array per map auto_per_realization, cross_per_realization, true_auto_per_realization the power of the posterior mean, its cross power with the truth and the power of the truth, one array per map burn_in, n_chains, n_used the burn-in removed, the chains per map and the iterations kept per chain

It also records the seeds, the map size, the resolution, the noise settings, the data type and the cosmology of the run.

docs.title: Using the result
docs.text:
Pass the merged file to the Fisher forecast as its lensing noise, together with a delensed covariance:

python -m cmb_lensing.fisher_forecast --noise 5 --delensed_covariance <delensed_covariance.npz> --phi_noise sampler_phi_noise.npz

The forecast must use the same data type (--pol) as the run that produced the file. The same file can be given to the delensed covariance pipeline (see Computing Delensed Covariance Matrices).

docs.title: Plotting the phi noise spectra
docs.text:
One script plots this noise next to the noise of the MAP estimates, as a function of scale:

python measure_phi_noise/phi_noise_analysis.py

The paths of the two merged files and the map settings are set at the bottom of the script. The plots compare both noise levels with the theory spectrum of the lensing potential and with the quadratic-estimate noise, and are written into this folder:

measure_phi_noise/phi_noise_plots/noise_level_<noise>uk/
